title: Ten Days Erased from the Calendar: Europe Leaps from Thursday to Friday
summary: Tells how the eleven-minute error the Julian calendar built up every year pushed Easter out of spring, and how in fifteen eighty-two Pope Gregory the Thirteenth cut ten days from the calendar, so that the day after Thursday the fourth of October became Friday the fifteenth of October. The episode ranges from the calculations of Luigi Lilio and Clavius to the centuries of Protestant resistance, Sweden's thirtieth of February, Britain losing eleven days in seventeen fifty-two, and the reform reaching Russia, Greece and Türkiye only in the twentieth century.
